title: Behind a censorship firewall: no VPN

points.text: The Behind-Firewall stack (earlier in the course, Behind-GFW, after China's Great Firewall) fits anywhere AI services are closed by state filtering or by the vendors themselves.
Without a VPN in mainland China, Claude, OpenAI, most AI IDEs, AI Studio, and Hugging Face are unavailable; GitHub and npm need mirrors.

Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini (AI Studio) are closed to Russia by the companies themselves: they don't serve users in Russia, and a VPN doesn't change that — signing in through a VPN breaks their terms, and accounts get banned.

children.heading: How to recognise a firewall by its symptoms

points.text: A firewall gives itself away like this: the TCP connection to the server is established, but the TLS handshake times out, and it happens on several domains of the same service at once.

outline.heading: ⚡ Quick install of the Behind-Firewall stack (one line)

points.text: One command installs the LiteLLM proxy and the Hermes agent (with the official Nous Research installer), writes a ready config (Cerebras + Gemini Flash), and connects Hermes to the model gateway.

outline.heading: Step 2: Google Gemini Flash (backup for longer tasks)

points.text: Download model (via HuggingFace mirror) in China: https://hf-mirror.com replaces huggingface.co.
The course agent is Hermes (NousResearch/hermes-agent) — the one the author uses.
